reviewer.role: independent bounded CODE-PROOF input-cap and retained-I/O reviewer

verdict: R10 closes R9-INPUT-CAP-NAMES-008 at the design level: it preserves R7's eight materialized public keys, defines max_request_input_bytes and max_observe_input_bytes as fixed non-materialized parser caps, and separates max_request_bytes from raw request admission. Two contract details remain under-specified before schema/profile freeze: the complete raw-input error context must explicitly bind its fixed limit value, and max_bundle_bytes must identify whether observed bytes are the canonical saved bundle envelope (including LF) or a supplied raw manifest domain. The cap+1 retained read strategy is finite and feasible when implemented through one retained input descriptor with the existing final lineage priority.
scope: Read-only review of R10 against R7, R9 and the immutable R9 independent closure review, focused on raw fixed-cap names, saved-cap domains, exact error naming/pointer/limit/observed semantics, and retained-I/O feasibility. No source, schema, test, fixture, Git, provider, network, connector, Vault or Grok mutation.

closure_matrix.evidence: R10 lines 3-5 preserves R7's eight-field limits.public map; lines 7-21 bind fixed request/observe raw caps, names, /input pointer, pre-decode priority and bounded cap+1 observation; lines 23-40 binds max_request_bytes exclusively to the complete sealed request envelope; lines 42-53 separates observe saved envelopes and bundle/body domains. This directly supplies the fixed-constant and saved-request mapping missing from the R9 finding.
closure_matrix.cross_check: R7 lines 38-60; R9 lines 33-75; R9 review finding R9-INPUT-CAP-NAMES-008

closure_matrix.title: Fixed raw-cap errors do not explicitly bind the required limit field/value
closure_matrix.evidence: R9 lines 67-75 require CODE_PROOF_LIMIT_EXCEEDED details exactly {instance_pointer, limit_name, limit, observed} and strict integer limit and observed values. R10 lines 9-12 bind name/pointer and lines 17-19 bind observed=cap+1 on excess, but never state the complete raw error object or that limit equals the fixed 65536/1048576 constant. The saved request example at lines 28-33 is exact, making the omission for the two fixed errors material.
closure_matrix.required_closure: State exact contexts for request and observe raw overflow, including limit=max_request_input_bytes constant or 65536 and limit=max_observe_input_bytes constant or 1048576, observed=the bounded cap+1 prefix count, instance_pointer=/input, and the fixed names. Include equal/cap+1 vectors and the oversized-malformed-JSON precedence.

closure_matrix.title: max_bundle_bytes observed domain and pointer remain ambiguous
closure_matrix.evidence: R7 lines 140-149 calls the bundle input manifest a canonical saved envelope and says its output copy is byte-identical. R7 lines 53-60 state lowered saved caps apply to complete canonical envelope bytes including LF. R9 lines 67-75 closes serialized-cap errors but gives pointer examples that omit bundle. R10 lines 42-46 says max_bundle_bytes applies to a separately retained raw Git bundle manifest, without saying whether observed is complete canonical saved bytes (including LF) or supplied raw manifest bytes, and without an exact instance_pointer/context example.
closure_matrix.required_closure: Choose and state one domain. If it is the R7 saved-envelope domain, bind {instance_pointer:"/bundle", limit_name:"max_bundle_bytes", limit:<materialized cap>, observed:<complete canonical bytes including LF>}; if it is a raw supplied-manifest domain, state how that differs from the byte-identical canonical bundle file and its retained lineage. Add cap-1/equal/cap+1 and no-install vectors.

positive_constraints: Read at most cap+1 raw bytes before JSON decoding or embedded-limit access.
Use the bounded prefix count as observed; never drain the remainder merely to report total size.
Keep fixed raw-cap refusal ahead of decoder errors, while final unsafe-path/lineage verification retains priority.
Perform refusal before any output installation and assert unchanged output state.
required_implementation_evidence: One retained descriptor/identity must cover the bounded read and final lineage check; do not reopen by pathname after the cap decision.
The implementation must prove cap+1 is a byte count, not decoded characters or a stat-size trust decision.
For a replaced/uncheckable input edge, return existing WORK_PATH_UNSAFE precedence even when the raw cap was exceeded.
Persist no unbounded prefix and do not allocate the complete oversized input.
retained_io_review.r10_text_support: R10 lines 16-21 explicitly require bounded cap+1 reading and existing final lineage verification; the descriptor rule remains an implementation gate inherited from retained-I/O reviews.

required_next_closure: Add exact fixed raw-cap CODE_PROOF_LIMIT_EXCEEDED contexts with limit values.
Resolve max_bundle_bytes byte domain, pointer and observed-count semantics against the canonical saved-envelope rule.
Generate/profile-check error-name enums without adding the two fixed names to limits.public.
Run cap-1/equal/cap+1, malformed-oversize, whitespace-heavy, lowered-saved-request, bundle and no-install retained-lineage vectors.
